entries.title: E(a) and the exponent 7/2 read over the whole history (X7)
entries.what: Desk derivation, sympy and a full LCDM numeric check (x7_two_histories.py, x7_relative_growth.py).
entries.outcome: The rate accounting with n = 7/2 and the first law with the record term agree only at a = 1; over the history they disagree (n_eff = 19/2 + 1/a). E(a) rests on the record constraint, which is the balance law d ln E/d ln a = 1 - ln E (writer at one per e-fold, no eraser). The chains, which use E(a) as the record term's shape, are unchanged. Book: note added at eq:law_Sneed.

entries.title: Lambda's coefficient and the 18th chain (X8)
entries.what: The Lambda expression reduces to Omega_b/Omega_m = (3/16) sqrt(Omega_L); measured 0.1564 against 0.1551. Among 1,276 simple forms of the same kind, one matches this closely for a random target 69 % of the time; the 18th chain holds the relation to 1.0046 +/- 0.0068 but cannot supply the coefficient. The only unknown is the 2/pi; lead: the average projection of a direction in a surface onto one axis of it is 2/pi.

entries.title: IAM from the beginning (X22, X20, X21)
entries.what: Horizon fill at the end of inflation 3e-4, electroweak 3e-17, nucleosynthesis 9e-23, recombination 1e-29 (upper bounds). Early records written into the horizon's record term would act like a huge cosmological constant, so their absence is required: early costs are paid into the local thermal bath. X20: per Kiefer and Polarski (arXiv:0810.0087) super-horizon decoherence entropy is capped at half its maximum, the inflationary horizon about 1e-12 full. X21: the record term vanishes with the Weyl curvature, Penrose's smooth start.

entries.title: The cosmic record priced by bound structure (X7)
entries.what: Binding energy of all structure, final over today: 2.75 (Press-Schechter), 2.63 (Sheth-Tormen), c 0.97-1.02, but the past runs too steep. Counted at each halo's formation-epoch density the past follows exp(1 - 1/a) to within 8-17 % (Sheth-Tormen) back to z = 3, but the endpoint drops to c 0.63-0.67. The ten-number fit cannot tell c apart (chi-square 6.35 and 6.43 reproduced; growth points move under 0.5); the chains cannot separate the shapes (0.004 in growth suppression).

entries.title: Night checks on GitHub: the halves, the matter coupling and rule C (X1, X3, X6, X15, X18, X19, R13)
entries.what: 6:48 PM to 10:22 PM, sympy on GitHub. A paid hold keeps at most 1/3 of what it pays, settled at 50 digits (X3). Rule C (each sector at its own-density horizon temperature) gives exactly twice Hawking's temperature on a Schwarzschild black hole and is withdrawn with its beta_m = Omega_m^(3/2). Matter in the Hubble sphere priced as its own black hole at Hawking's temperature holds the Smarr half, Omega_m/2 (X6, lead); Lambda's sqrt(Omega_L) is its own horizon's de Sitter temperature, leaving one factor 16/3 (X8). At its own temperature a surface holds kappa R/c^2 of its energy: 1 de Sitter, 1/2 black hole (X1). The 4 Omega_m threshold is a crossing time of 2 Omega_m Hubble times (X15); a particle on its own Compton sphere balances its rest energy with the Bekenstein count 2 pi (X19); the book's matter rate is matter's own congruence feeling the record (X18).

entries.title: The cosmic M number and local-to-horizon migration (X7)
entries.what: The typical collapsing halo's cosmic M grows close to E(a)^2 for every overdensity definition tried; its square root is a Mach number, the virial speed over the thermal speed at the horizon's temperature. Migrating local records to the horizon delays the record without changing its shape (exponent spread 3.3 to 3.0, mean 3.9 to about 4.3).

sections.heading: What we learned that we did not know yesterday

entries.title: The eraser is not the cell's proofreading
entries.what: Without TET erasers stray marks rise 0.985-1.292 of wild type in five knockout units, not the 48-81 times a discard step needs; the floor's form 1/(1+e^M) is Sartori and Pigolotti's one-step copy limit.

entries.title: The within-sample slope replicates; the across-type rise does not follow
entries.what: PHY-087 step 2 in the blind-test laboratory: median 1.03 (0.34-1.67) of the derived form at 50,000-CpG tiles; across types the level rises 2.4 times faster than the formula (0.1377 against 0.0584), so each type's level (A8) needs something else.

entries.title: E(a)'s shape rests on the record constraint alone
entries.what: The 7/2 rate accounting and the first law agree only at a = 1; the chains' fits are untouched because they use E(a) as a shape.

entries.title: All matter writes the cosmic record, and halos cannot supply beta_m one by one
entries.what: R4: baryons only (Omega_b/2 = 0.025) is excluded at 4.5 sigma within the dual-sector reading of the local Hubble rates. X6: collapsed structure's kinetic energy is 2.6e-8 to 2.6e-6 of the critical energy; the size Omega_m/2 sits at the horizon scale.

entries.title: Every settled horizon holds 1/2 of what it paid
entries.what: Black hole and cosmic horizon alike, against the price paid as the area grew; a paid pump keeps at most 1/3.

sections.heading: Our own mistakes, and what caught each

entries.title: Decoder names changed without the author's words
entries.what: Four chain names were renamed in the Decoder on an unexecuted plan item; reverted the same day. Caught by the author.

entries.title: X7 worked from memory
entries.what: Evening toy models were built without reading X7's own register row and the book's derivation; marked superseded. Caught by the author.

entries.title: Referee labels in exploration
entries.what: A lead was marked post hoc during exploration; the rule now is that a result is a lead with its open step until the final test. Caught by the author.

entries.title: Smaller slips corrected the same day
entries.what: A DNMT1 literature entry was a Dnmt3a paper (the reviewer); an end-state review table showed stale glossary text (the reviewer); a 1.24 near-match came from comparing entropy with energy (found in the next check); a far-future sentence not in the author's words had stood in four places (the author).

entries.title: Writing on the nearest surface
entries.what: The author's picture: every record is written locally first on its nearest 2D encoding surface (the chromatin for a cell, the surface around a star or halo), pushing out the local fabric; a black hole forms when a local surface saturates; the horizon receives what migrates out. The book's saturation chapter already carries the two-entry ledger.

entries.title: The cosmic record and the cell's balance law
entries.what: E(a) is the cell's balance law with no eraser; the book's 'M solved with feedback' integration is the route to its size (R8).

entries.title: Exploration is free
entries.what: Desk math, toy models and forecasts on spent data carry no seal, no referee label and no pass or fail; seals, synthetics, canaries and data-spend rules apply only to final derivation tests.

entries.title: Read the row and the book first
entries.what: Before any row is worked: its full register entry, its neighbours, and every book section it names; nothing from memory.
